name: Jaiphal
traditionalUses: Poor sleep (a pinch in warm milk)
kitchenUse: A tiny pinch grated into warm milk, kheer or garam masala.

typicalUse.adultAmount: A pinch only; never more than food amounts

cautions.note: Avoid more than a culinary pinch in pregnancy.
Keep whole nutmeg away from children; swallowing even one or two teaspoons can cause poisoning.
Large amounts (around two teaspoons or more) can cause a racing heart, confusion, vomiting and hallucinations from myristicin.

interactions.effect: Large amounts may add to drowsiness from sleeping pills.

evidence.summary: Traditional use only for digestion and sleep. Poisoning from large amounts is well documented.

sources.title: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part I
